meta.description: Evidence ledger for the chapter-wise Polity PYQ sheet. 'row' is the question number as printed in Polity_PYQ_Laxmikanth_Chapterwise.pdf and in the 'Q. No.' column of the workbook (worksheet row = row + 2). 'verified_key' is always expressed against the option order printed in this sheet, never against the booklet order of the original paper.
meta.method: Question text and the sheet's own option list were matched to published solved papers / official keys; the correct *option text* was identified first and only then mapped to a letter in this sheet's ordering.

statuses.confirmed: Printed key agrees with the published answer.
statuses.corrected: Printed key was wrong; verified_key replaces it.
statuses.resolved: Source printed an ambiguous key (*, A/C); resolved from a web source.
statuses.defect: Question or options are corrupt/defective in the source; no single defensible answer.
statuses.deleted: BPSC deleted the question from evaluation; it has no answer.

kgs_audit.note: Random read-through of twelve KGS-book rows (Q42, 47, 55, 69, 122, 154, 235, 268, 296, 447, 462, 498). Q47 was wrong and is corrected below; Q296 was plausible but not confirmed; Q498 has a corrupt option table. The other nine matched the constitutional position.

json_random_sample.note: Uniform random sample of eight JSON-derived rows drawn after the conflict rows were fixed, to measure the error rate without the conflict-selection bias: 3 of 8 wrong (Q37, Q283, Q301), 5 right.

entries.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 42nd Amendment
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q102 (Series A): 'The correct answer is (C) 2 and 3'; concurred by licchavilyceum.com 69th solved paper.

entries.q: What is the name of the 10 conduct orders of the 42nd constitutional amendment
entries.evidence: '42nd Amendment Act, 1976 | Added Socialist, Secular, Integrity to Preamble; added Fundamental Duties' — ten Fundamental Duties in the new Part IVA (Art. 51A).

entries.q: By which constitutional amendment have the fundamental duties been added
entries.evidence: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added the Fundamental Duties (Part IVA).

entries.q: A new chapter has been added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment
entries.evidence: The new chapter is Part IVA on Fundamental Duties, inserted by the 42nd Amendment.

entries.q: Fundamental duties laid down
entries.evidence: Same: Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 (on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation).

entries.q: Which of the following is a fundamental duty in India
entries.verified_text: To preserve the rich heritage of our mixed culture
entries.evidence: Art. 51A(f): duty 'to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture'.

entries.q: The legislative origins of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act
entries.evidence: 'The legislative origin of such Amendment dates back to the Constitution (64th Amendment) Bill introduced by Rajiv Gandhi in July 1989'.

entries.q: Size of Council of Ministers has been restricted to 15 percent
entries.evidence: 'The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 ... restricted the size of the council of ministers ... to 15 percent'.

entries.q: Creation of a new state requires a majority
entries.evidence: Article 3: 'Parliament, by a simple majority, can enact laws to form a new state'.

entries.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment traces back to which earlier Bill
entries.evidence: Same 64th Amendment Bill of July 1989 as Q7 (duplicate row).

entries.q: The minimum age for contesting elections to the Panchayati Raj
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC Q7: 'Ans: (A)'; testbook (68th Set B official paper) also gives 21 years.

entries.q: Which Amendment to the Constitution abolished the two seats
entries.evidence: 'The 104th Amendment Act, 2019 abolished the provision for nominating members from the Anglo-Indian community' (Article 334).

entries.q: In which provision is the provision for amendment of the constitutional
entries.evidence: 'Part XX includes only Article 368. This Article grants Parliament the constituent power to amend any provision of the Constitution'.

entries.q: What kind of majority is required for constitutional amendment to create a new state?
entries.evidence: Art. 3 read with Art. 4(2): a bill for a new State 'is passed by a simple majority in Parliament' and is 'not a constitutional amendment'.

entries.q: By which constitutional amendment Delhi was named National Capital Territory
entries.evidence: 'The amendment transformed the Union Territory of Delhi into the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi' (Arts 239AA/239AB, 1991).

entries.q: A bill can be brought to amend the Indian Constitution
entries.verified_text: Either in the Lok Sabha or in the Rajya Sabha
entries.evidence: 'A constitutional amendment bill can only be initiated by the introduction of a bill in either House of Parliament, not in state legislatures'.

entries.q: First Amendment Act Bill for the Indian Constitution was brought in
entries.evidence: 'The Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951 ... Nehru ... moved on May 10 of that year, and Parliament passed it on June 18'.

entries.q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Act was called Mini Constitution?
entries.evidence: 'The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 ... Often called the "Mini-Constitution"'.

entries.q: Regarding the 42nd Amendment of the Indian Constitution, consider the following statements: 1. It added three words 'socialism' in the preamble - 'Secular' and 'integrity'. 2. It added eight fundamental duties
entries.evidence: Statement 1 is right (Socialist, Secular, Integrity) but 2 is wrong (ten, not eight, Fundamental Duties) and 3 is wrong (Art. 48A, not Art. 47) — the printed key (d) '2 and 3' is the only option that fits.

entries.q: Which one of the following characteristics is not true for unitary form of Government
entries.evidence: Unitary government is 'suitable for small countries' and 'not suitable for big countries' — so 'ideal for large countries' is the untrue statement.

entries.q: Match the following : I. Union List II. State list III. Concurrent list
entries.evidence: The three matching pairs and the item list were lost in extraction — the options read only 'a b c', 'a c b', 'c a b', 'c b a', so no answer can be defended from this text.

entries.q: In which one of the following years was Sarkaria Commission, which was constituted to examine Centre-State relations, set up / report submitted
entries.evidence: Sarkaria was appointed on 9 June 1983 but submitted its final report in October 1987 — the year the sheet's option (d) gives.

entries.q: Consider the following subjects belonging to different lists of the constitution of India. Which of the following subjects belong to concurrent list? 1) Protection of wildlife 2) Income on Agriculture 3) Tax on Electricity 4) Price control
entries.evidence: List III has '17-B. Protection of wild animals and birds' and '34. Price control'; income from agriculture (List II, Entry 46) and taxes on electricity (List II, Entry 53) are State subjects.

entries.q: In which of the following years, the Sarkaria Commission gave its report
entries.evidence: 'Sarkaria Commission ... submitted its report in 1987' (duplicate of Q22).

entries.q: Match- I. Federal List A. 97 entries II. State list B. 47 entries III. concurrent list C. 66 entries
entries.evidence: 'Union List | 97 subjects; State List | 66 subjects; Concurrent List | 47 subjects' → I-A, II-C, III-B.

entries.q: Land reform is under subject
entries.evidence: List II (State List) Entry 18: 'Land, that is to say, rights in or over land, land tenures ... land improvement'.

entries.q: In which list of the Indian Constitution are the formats of 'oath or affirmation' given
entries.evidence: 'Third | Forms of oaths and affirmations' — the Third Schedule (Arts 75(4), 99, 124(6), 188, 219).

entries.q: Which of the following subjects is in the concurrent list
entries.evidence: 'The 42nd Amendment (1976) moved Education, Forests, Weights and Measures ... from the State List to the Concurrent List'.

entries.q: Which of the following is not included in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution
entries.evidence: The 29 listed subjects include libraries, fuel & fodder and technical training, but there is no entry for rural sports.

entries.q: Prevention of cruelty to animals has been placed in which list
entries.evidence: 'List III: Concurrent List — 17. Prevention of cruelty to animals'.

entries.q: Which of the following Schedules of the Indian Constitution contains provisions regarding allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha
entries.evidence: 'Fourth | Allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to states and UTs' (Arts 4(1), 80(2)).

entries.q: The Fifth Schedule deals with the protection of the rights and interests of
entries.evidence: 'Fifth | Administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes (other than NE)' — Art. 244(1).

entries.q: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution is related to
entries.evidence: 'Tenth | Anti-defection provisions' (Arts 102(2), 191(2)); added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985.

entries.q: President of India exercises his powers
entries.verified_text: either directly or through officers subordinate to him
entries.evidence: Article 53(1): executive power 'shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him'.

entries.q: Emmerson Mnangagwa was elected as the President of which country
entries.evidence: 'Emmerson Mnangagwa has been sworn in as president of Zimbabwe' on 24 November 2017.

entries.q: The Indian President is eligible for re-election
entries.evidence: 67th BPSC: 'The President of India is eligible to be re-elected for any number of times. Ans: (C)' in that page's own option order (Twice/Thrice/Any number/Once).

entries.q: Who was the candidate of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) in 15th Presidential Election
entries.evidence: 'Yashwant Sinha was the candidate of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) in the 15th Presidential Election in India' (2022).

entries.q: The President of India inaugurated 'PARAM KAMRUPA' Supercomputer
entries.evidence: PIB: the President 'inaugurated Supercomputer facility Param-Kamrupa ... at IIT Guwahati' on 13 October 2022.

entries.q: Among the following who has been Speaker of Lok Sabha prior to his Election as President
entries.evidence: Reddy was elected Speaker of the Sixth Lok Sabha on 26 March 1977 and resigned a few months later to contest the July 1977 presidential election.

entries.q: The Executive Head of India is
entries.evidence: 'Executive Headship | Article 52 & Article 53 | Formal executive head (de jure)' — the President.

entries.q: Executive power vested in the Central Government by the Constitution has been given to
entries.evidence: 'Article 53 — Executive power of the Union vests in the President'.

entries.q: President-
entries.evidence: 'the President is part of Parliament. Under Article 79, Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses'.

entries.q: The Supreme Commander of the Indian Defense Force is
entries.evidence: Article 53(2): the President is 'supreme commander of the armed forces'.

entries.q: The President of India exercises his powers
entries.verified_text: Directly or through his subordinate officers
entries.evidence: Article 53(1): power 'shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him' (duplicate of Q34).

entries.q: How many times is the President of India eligible for re-election
entries.evidence: 'Article 57: Eligible for re-election for any number of terms. Contrast with US 22nd Amendment'.

entries.q: Who are included in the 'Electoral College' of the President of India
entries.verified_text: All elected members of both the Houses of Parliament and all elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
entries.evidence: 'Article 54 — Electoral College: Elected MPs (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha) + Elected MLAs of States + Delhi & Puducherry' — none of (a)-(c) alone.

entries.q: In India, the President is elected by.
entries.evidence: Article 54: the electoral college consists of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies — option (d). The printed key E ('None of the above') contradicts an option that is present.

entries.q: In India, the President is elected by-
entries.evidence: Article 55(3): election is by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. Options (b) and (c) are both true and there is no 'both' option, so the printed question has no single answer.

entries.q: If there is any dispute in the election of the President of India, that is decided by whom
entries.evidence: 'Article 71(1) — Inquired and decided exclusively by the Supreme Court of India. Decision ... is final'.

entries.q: The President of India can be removed from his post by
entries.evidence: 'Impeachment | Article 61 | Passed by 2/3rds majority of total membership in both Houses' — not by the PM, Lok Sabha alone or the CJI.

entries.q: Executive powers of the Central Government in the Indian Constitution are vested in the
entries.evidence: Article 53: the executive power of the Union is vested in the President (exercised on ministerial advice).

entries.q: Consider the following statements regarding the President of India. 1. Article 53 mentions that the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President. 2. The President shall hold office for five years after assuming office. 3. Article 60 mentions the process of impeachment
entries.evidence: Statements 1 (Art. 53) and 2 (Art. 56, five-year term) are right; statement 3 is wrong — Art. 60 is the oath, impeachment is Art. 61.

entries.q: If the posts of President and Vice President are vacant, then who holds the office of President
entries.evidence: 'In case of the absence of the Vice President, the Chief Justice of India (or, in his absence, the senior most judge of the Supreme Court) will act ... as the President' (Art. 65).

entries.q: If the post of President of India is vacant and the Vice President and the Chief Justice are also unavailable
entries.verified_text: Senior judge of the Supreme Court
entries.evidence: Article 65(1): the Chief Justice, 'or, in his absence, the senior most judge of the Supreme Court', discharges the President's functions.

entries.q: The Indian Constitution does not give authority to the President of India to
entries.verified_text: Appointment of Chief Minister of the states
entries.evidence: The President appoints the PM (Art. 75) but a State's Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor (Art. 164) — so this power is not the President's.

entries.q: The President of India does not have the right to
entries.verified_text: Remove the judge of the Supreme Court
entries.evidence: A Supreme Court judge can only be removed by the Art. 124(4) process (address of both Houses) — the President has no unilateral power of removal.

entries.q: What is the order of Mrs. Pratibha Patil as the President of the Republic of India
entries.evidence: 'on 25 July 2007, took oath as India's 12th President, the first woman to hold the position'.

entries.q: India's first President Rajendra Prasad was from which state
entries.evidence: 'Rajendra Prasad ... Pioneer from Bihar and the 1st President of India' (born at Ziradei, Bihar).

entries.q: The first President of independent India was
entries.evidence: Same source: Rajendra Prasad, the 1st President, was from Bihar (duplicate of Q58).

entries.q: A Bill which is presented in the Parliament becomes an Act after which
entries.evidence: 'no bill becomes law without the President's assent' — assent under Art. 111 completes the legislative process.

entries.q: What is the capital of Paraguay
entries.evidence: 'The correct answer is Asuncion' — the Vice President visited Paraguay on 5-7 March 2019.

entries.q: Electoral College for the 16th Vice Presidential Election
entries.evidence: ECI press note: 'Electoral College comprises of a total of 788 members of both Houses of Parliament'.

entries.q: Arrange the following words in logical and meaningful order : 1. Vice President, 2. President, 3. Speaker, 4. Prime Minister, 5. Members of the Parliament
entries.evidence: Order of precedence: Rank 1 President, 2 Vice-President, 3 Prime Minister, 6 Speaker of the Lok Sabha, 21 Members of Parliament → 2,1,4,3,5.

entries.q: The Chairman of which assembly is not its member
entries.evidence: Article 89(1): the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and 'is not a member of the House'.

entries.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
entries.evidence: Article 89(1): the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

entries.q: Who is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha
entries.evidence: Article 89(1): the Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States.

entries.q: The Chairman of Rajya Sabha is
entries.evidence: Same provision as Q65/Q66 (Article 89(1)).

entries.q: Which statement is false
entries.verified_text: The Vice President is elected by the President of India
entries.evidence: Article 66: the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of both Houses, not by the President — so option (c) is the false statement.

entries.q: How many members are there in the electoral college for the 16th Vice President
entries.evidence: ECI: 233 + 12 Rajya Sabha + 543 Lok Sabha = 788 members.

entries.q: The number of Shri Mohammad Hamid Ansari as the Vice President
entries.evidence: List of Vice-Presidents: '12 — Mohammad Hamid Ansari, 2007-2017'.

entries.q: Constitution Day of India is celebrated on
entries.evidence: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949, 'a date now celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas)'.

entries.q: Indian National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly
entries.evidence: 'The design of the Indian National Flag was adopted by Constituent Assembly on 22nd July 1947'.

entries.q: Constitution Day of India is celebrated on
entries.evidence: Same fact as Q71 (duplicate row, different year suffix in the options).

entries.q: When did the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly take place
entries.evidence: 'The Constituent Assembly held its first sitting on 9 December 1946'.

entries.q: How much time did it take to make the Indian Constitution
entries.evidence: 'The Constituent Assembly of India took exactly 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days'.

entries.q: The decision to implement the Constitution on 26 January was taken because
entries.verified_text: Congress celebrated this date as Independence Day in 1930
entries.evidence: 26 January 1950 'was specifically chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration of 1930'.

entries.q: By whom was the Constitution of India adopted
entries.evidence: 'The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949' by the Constituent Assembly.

entries.q: The Indian Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly
entries.evidence: 'The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949'.

entries.q: The Indian Constitution was adopted
entries.evidence: The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly, which held its first sitting on 9 December 1946.

entries.q: Indian Constitution Day is celebrated on
entries.evidence: The adoption date, 26 November 1949, 'is now celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas)'.

entries.q: On August 29, 1947, the Constitution Writing Committee was formed, whose chairman was Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and six others — who was not a member
entries.evidence: Members were Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, K.M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadulla, B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan — Nehru was not on the Drafting Committee.

entries.q: Consider the following statements about Central Government: 1. Ministries and Departments are formed by the Prime Minister with consultation of the Cabinet Secretary. 2. Every Minister is allocated a Ministry by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
entries.evidence: 'Statement 1 is incorrect: Ministries and Departments are created ... by the President ... under the Allocation of Business Rules ... Statement 2 is correct'.

entries.q: Who was the Prime Minister of England when the Montague-Chelmsford Act was passed in 1919
entries.evidence: 'Lloyd George was the Prime Minister of England when the Montague-Chelmsford Act was passed in 1919'.

entries.q: The Prime Minister of India is responsible to whom
entries.evidence: Article 75(3): 'the ministry is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha'; the PM heads it.

entries.q: On February 20, 1947, Prime Minister Attlee announced the British Government's decision to withdraw from India latest by
entries.evidence: UPI, 20 Feb 1947: Attlee told the Commons the transfer of power would be effected 'by a date not later than June, 1948'.

entries.q: The Prime Minister of India is
entries.evidence: The PM is appointed by the President as 'the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha' and heads the Union (Central) Government — Art. 75.

entries.q: Usually the Prime Minister of India is
entries.evidence: By convention the President appoints 'the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha as Prime Minister'; a minister must be a member of either House.

entries.q: To whom is the Prime Minister of India answerable
entries.evidence: Article 75 note: 'the entire Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, must maintain the confidence of the Lok Sabha'.

entries.q: Ministers of the Union Council of Ministers are collectively responsible
entries.evidence: Article 75(3): all ministers 'are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha'; option (c) 'Parliament' is the looser answer, (d) names the House the Constitution names.

entries.q: The Council of Ministers is responsible
entries.evidence: Article 75(3): the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (a House of Parliament); option (d) is the only defensible choice.

entries.q: In the Indian political system, the executive works under subordination
entries.evidence: Parliamentary system: 'the executive is directly accountable to the legislature'; the cabinet is drawn from and sits in the legislature.

entries.q: By which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts, the number of Council of Ministers
entries.evidence: 'The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 ... restricted the size of the council of ministers ... to 15 percent'.

entries.q: Who has recently been given the charge of the Ministry of Minority Affairs
entries.evidence: Rashtrapati Bhavan, 6 July 2022: Smriti Zubin Irani 'be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Minority Affairs' after Naqvi's resignation.

entries.q: Which Article of the Constitution restrict a Member of Parliament to hold the office of profit
entries.evidence: 'Article 102(1)(a) ... makes the holding of an office of profit by a member of Parliament a ground for disqualification'.

entries.q: How many members are elected from Bihar to the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: 'There are 40 Lok Sabha constituencies in the Indian state of Bihar'.

entries.q: Which officer of the Government of India has the right to take part in the proceedings of Parliament
entries.evidence: Article 88: 'Every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of either House'.

entries.q: What is the minimum age for a Member of the Parliament
entries.evidence: Article 84(b): not less than 30 years for the Council of States and 'not less than twenty-five years of age' for the House of the People.

entries.q: Money Bill can be presented
entries.evidence: 'A money bill, unlike other bills, can only be introduced in the Lower House, that is, the Lok Sabha and not the Rajya Sabha. Article 109(1) expressly forbids' it.

entries.q: Who is the Ex Officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
entries.evidence: Article 89(1): the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

entries.q: The Parliament of which of the following nations dismissed the honorary citizenship of Aung San Suu Kyi in 2018
entries.evidence: 28 Sept 2018: 'Canadian MPs have voted unanimously to revoke the honorary citizenship of ... Aung San Suu Kyi'; Canada granted it in 2007, Norway never did.

entries.q: In order to be chosen a member of the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q94: 'Answer. C'; testbook 64th official paper confirms 25 years.

entries.q: In which Article of the Constitution of India was the provision for reservation of scheduled castes in the Lok Sabha made
entries.evidence: 'Article 330- Reservation of seats for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes in the House of people'.

entries.q: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding parliamentary form of Government
entries.evidence: In a parliamentary system 'the executive is responsible to the legislature' — the reverse of options (a)-(c) and unrelated to (d), so (e) is the only defensible choice.

entries.q: The division of each State into territorial constituencies for the Lok Sabha is done by the Delimitation Commission. This delimitation has been freezed till which year
entries.evidence: 'The Constitution (Eighty-Fourth Amendment) Act, 2001 further extended the freeze until after the first census following the year 2026'.

entries.q: Generally how many sessions are there in the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: 'By convention, three sessions are held annually — Budget, Monsoon, and Winter'.

entries.q: The representation in the Rajya Sabha includes
entries.verified_text: More than one of the above
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC final answer key, Q5: 'Answer: D' — nominated members and indirectly elected members both qualify.

entries.q: What is the object of "cut motion" in Parliament
entries.verified_text: To move a proposal to reduce expenditure in the budget proposals
entries.evidence: 'The correct answer is to reduce expenditure in the Budget proposals'; a cut motion is a motion to reduce the amount of a demand for a grant.

entries.q: What is the position of representation of Anglo-Indian Community in Lok Sabha
entries.verified_text: Nomination of them has been done away with by 104th Constitutional Amendment
entries.evidence: 'The 104th Amendment Act, 2019 abolished the provision for nominating members from the Anglo-Indian community'.

entries.q: After elections to the 18th Lok Sabha, who was appointed as the Union Minister of Textiles
entries.evidence: PTI, 11 June 2024: 'Senior Bihar BJP MP Giriraj Singh, who retained the Begusarai Lok Sabha seat ... took charge as the Union Textiles Minister'.

entries.q: In which Lok Sabha seat, one of India's PVTGs, Shompen tribe, for the first time exercised their democratic right to vote in April 2024
entries.evidence: 'For the first time in Andaman and Nicobar Islands, seven members of the Shompen tribe ... exercised their voting rights for the lone Lok Sabha seat in the union territory' (19 April 2024).

entries.q: The minimum age limit for a person to be elected in an election to the Lok Sabha is
entries.evidence: Article 84(b): 25 years for the House of the People.

entries.q: What age should a person not be below to be elected as a member of the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: Article 84(b): 25 years for the House of the People.

entries.q: What is the minimum age to become a Member of Parliament
entries.evidence: Article 84(b): 25 years (Lok Sabha) / 30 years (Rajya Sabha); the sheet's options only offer 25.

entries.q: State-wise allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha is based on the 1971 census. Till how many years will this determination continue
entries.evidence: The 1971-census allocation was frozen by the 42nd Amendment and 'extended until after the first census following the year 2026' by the 84th.

entries.q: Lok Sabha seats in each state are determined by the Delimitation Commission. This delimitation has been stopped till
entries.evidence: Same 84th Amendment freeze — the 2002 Commission redrew boundaries but not state seat shares.

entries.q: The allocation of seats for each state in the present Lok Sabha is based on
entries.evidence: 'The total number of Lok Sabha seats and the inter-State allocation ... have remained fixed at their 1971-census levels'.

entries.q: Who has the power to nominate members from the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: 'Under Article 331, the President use to nominate 2 members of the Lok Sabha from the Anglo-Indians Community'.

entries.q: The Lok Sabha can be dissolved before the expiry of its term
entries.verified_text: By the President, on the advice of the Council of Ministers
entries.evidence: Rashtrapati Bhavan: the President dissolved the 16th Lok Sabha 'on the recommendation of the Union Cabinet', using Art. 85(2)(b).

entries.q: Lok Sabha can be dissolved before the completion of its term
entries.verified_text: By the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister
entries.evidence: Dissolution is on the Cabinet's advice (here the PM's recommendation), not at the President's discretion — so (d), not (a).

entries.q: How many sessions are there normally in the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: 'By convention, three sessions are held annually — Budget, Monsoon, and Winter'.

entries.q: At least how many sessions of the Lok Sabha are called
entries.evidence: Article 85: no more than six months may pass between two sessions, which forces at least two sittings a year.

entries.q: There should be maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament
entries.evidence: Article 85: 'the gap between two sessions must not exceed six months'.

entries.q: Which state sends the maximum number of representatives to the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: 1971-census allocation: Uttar Pradesh 85 seats, the largest of any state.

entries.q: As far as representation in the Lok Sabha is concerned, which states are in the second and third ranks
entries.evidence: 1971-census allocation: Bihar 54 and Maharashtra 48, behind Uttar Pradesh's 85 (West Bengal 42).

entries.q: A candidate for Lok Sabha elections loses his deposit if he cannot get
entries.evidence: 'the deposit has to be forfeited ... if the number of valid votes polled by the candidate is less than 1/6th' — not 1/3, 1/4 or 1/5, so (d).

entries.q: When were the first general elections of the Lok Sabha held
entries.evidence: 'The first general elections in our country took place between October 25, 1951, and February 21, 1952'.

entries.q: When was the Ninth Lok Sabha dissolved
entries.evidence: Table of Lok Sabhas: Ninth — commenced 18 December 1989, dissolved 13 March 1991.

entries.q: Elections for the 12th Lok Sabha were held in India
entries.evidence: Table of prematurely dissolved Houses: 12th Lok Sabha, start of term March 1998 — i.e. the general election was held in February 1998.

entries.q: Who is the leader of Lok Sabha?
entries.evidence: 'the current prime minister Narendra Modi has been serving as the leader of the house since 2014' — the PM is the Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha.

entries.q: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by
entries.verified_text: By all the members of the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: The Speaker is 'chosen by the House' — an elected member of the Lok Sabha elected by the Lok Sabha (Art. 93), not by the whole Parliament.

entries.q: Money Bill can be introduced by
entries.evidence: 'A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha ... It cannot originate in the Rajya Sabha'.

entries.q: Who presides over the joint session of Parliament
entries.evidence: Article 108: 'The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the sitting'; in his absence the Deputy Speaker, then the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

entries.q: An M.P. The seat of a Speaker can be declared vacant if he remains continuously absent from the House
entries.evidence: Article 101(4): absent 'for a period of sixty days' without permission — i.e. two months.

entries.q: Rajya Sabha consists of
entries.verified_text: 250 members, of whom 12 members are nominated by the President of India
entries.evidence: Rajya Sabha's own site: 'Article 80 ... lays down the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha as 250, out of which 12 members are nominated by the President and 238 are representatives of the States'.

entries.q: Representation in the Rajya Sabha includes
entries.verified_text: More than one of the above
entries.evidence: The Rajya Sabha combines members 'nominated by the President' (Art. 80(1)(a)) with members 'elected by the elected members of State Assemblies' (Art. 80(1)(b)) — so more than one option is right.

entries.q: According to Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, what is included in the definition of Money Bill?

entries.q: At present, who is the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (as on the exam date)
entries.evidence: Same fact: Urjit Patel, 24th RBI Governor, Sept 2016 – Dec 2018 (duplicate of Q279).

entries.q: The Governor of a State is appointed by
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q95: 'Answer. C' (Article 155).

entries.q: Who was the first Indian Governor of Bihar
entries.evidence: In 1920 Sinha 'was appointed as the first governor of the Province of Bihar and Orissa' and was the first Indian to hold the post.

entries.q: Who among the following was the first Governor of Bihar
entries.evidence: Table: '1 | Sir James David Sifton | 1 April 1936 | 10 March 1937' — first Governor of the new Bihar province.

entries.q: Who is the constitutional head of the executive head of the state government
entries.evidence: 'The Governor is the constitutional head of a state — the analogue of the President at the state level' (Arts 153-154).

entries.q: The Governor of a state is appointed by
entries.evidence: 'Article 155 | Appointment of Governor by the President'.

entries.q: On whose advice is 'President's Rule' usually imposed in the state
entries.evidence: 'the Governor ... may advise the President to declare President's Rule' under Arts 355-356, by sending a report.

entries.q: Who appoints the Governor of Jammu and Kashmir
entries.evidence: Article 155 applies to every State, including Jammu and Kashmir since 2019 — the Governor is appointed by the President.

entries.q: The authority to determine the number of Judges in a High Court
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q106: 'The correct answer is (A) The President' (Article 216 — the President fixes the number of High Court judges; Parliament does this only for the Supreme Court).

entries.q: Who among the following has the authority to determine the number of judges in the High Court
entries.evidence: Article 216: every High Court consists of a Chief Justice 'and such other judges as the President may ... deem necessary to appoint'.

entries.q: A High Court Judge addresses his resignation letter to
entries.evidence: 'Under Article 217(1)(a) of the Constitution, a High Court judge may resign by writing under his hand addressed to the President of India'.

entries.q: Which of the following High Courts is for more than one State
entries.evidence: The Gauhati High Court has jurisdiction over Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Mizoram.

entries.q: The Babri Masjid Ram Janmabhoomi dispute which is before the Allahabad High Court (Lucknow Bench) is a type of
entries.evidence: 'On September 30, 2010, the Allahabad High Court delivered its judgment in the title case' — the Ayodhya litigation is a civil title suit, not a mandamus or compensation claim.

entries.q: The Cabinet Mission came to India in
entries.evidence: 'The Cabinet Mission ... reached Delhi on 24 March 1946' — not on any of the 1942 dates offered in the options.

entries.q: Who was not the member of the Cabinet Mission
entries.evidence: Members were 'Pethick Lawrence ... Stafford Cripps ... and A.V. Alexander'; Wavell was the Viceroy and only 'participated in some of the discussions'.

entries.q: Who among the following was not a member of the Cabinet Mission
entries.evidence: 'the mission consisted of three Cabinet ministers: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A. V. Alexander' — Ramsay MacDonald was not on it.

entries.q: The Cabinet Mission was sent to India for which of the following? 1. To establish a national government 2. To work out a constitutional arrangement for the transfer of power 3. To work out the details of Jinnah's demand for Pakistan
entries.verified_text: More than one of the above
entries.evidence: The Mission aimed at 'transferring power to India, proposing an interim government, and establishing a constituent assembly' and it 'rejected the Muslim League's demand for a separate Pakistan' — 1 and 2 true, 3 false.

entries.q: Who among the following was not the member of the Cabinet Mission
entries.evidence: Pethick Lawrence and A.V. Alexander were both members; 'J. Andrew' was not part of the three-minister mission, so (c) is the correct choice.

entries.q: Which Article gives the list of 29 functions to be performed by the Panchayati Raj Institutions
entries.evidence: Article 243G read with the Eleventh Schedule: 'The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 areas in which Panchayats can exercise their responsibilities'.

entries.q: What is the main purpose of Panchayati Raj?
entries.verified_text: To enable people to participate in development administration
entries.evidence: Panchayati Raj is 'democratic decentralisation' meant to 'empower local communities' by transferring the 29 Eleventh-Schedule subjects to elected bodies.

entries.q: A Panchayat Samiti at the block level in India is only a/an
entries.evidence: 'A Panchayat Samiti at the block level in India is only a Coordinating and Supervisory Authority' — matches the printed key (c).

entries.q: Which one of the following Committees/Commissions recommended the creation of Nyaya Panchayats
entries.evidence: 'The correct answer is Ashok Mehta Committee ... recommended the creation of Nyaya Panchayats' (report, August 1978).

entries.q: The system of Panchayati Raj is mentioned in
entries.evidence: 'Local government', including Panchayati Raj, is Entry 5 of List II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule.

entries.q: Which one of the following Articles directs the State Governments to organize the Panchayats
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q98: 'Answer. B' (Article 40, DPSP).

entries.q: Which of the following was constituted under the Panchayati Raj system
entries.evidence: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX, creating the constitutional three-tier structure whose base is the Gram Panchayat at village level.

entries.q: Which Article lists the 29 functions of Panchayati Raj institutions
entries.evidence: Article 243G with the Eleventh Schedule: 'lists 29 areas in which Panchayats can exercise their responsibilities'.

entries.q: Which State does not have Panchayat system
entries.verified_text: None of the above / More than one of the above
entries.evidence: Article 243M: Part IX 'does not apply to the States of Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram' — three of the listed states, so 'more than one of the above'.

entries.q: To review the financial position of Panchayats
entries.evidence: 67th BPSC: 'The state government constitutes a finance commission every five years' (Article 243-I).

entries.q: Consider the following statements : In the post-73rd Amendment era
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC final key, Q4: 'Answer: B' — the 73rd Amendment does not decentralise judicial powers.

entries.q: At what level does a Panchayat Samiti operate
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC (Set B official paper) Q9: 'Block-level body'; the sheet's own note already recorded the conflict.

entries.q: Under Article "243J" which of the following can make provisions
entries.evidence: 70th BPSC PT: 'Correct Answer: b) State Legislature' — Article 243J.

entries.q: Who is empowered to review financial position of the Panchayats
entries.evidence: Article 243-I: 'the Governor shall constitute state finance commission every five years to review the financial position of the panchayats'.

entries.q: Community development program started
entries.evidence: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee was appointed in 1957 to examine the Community Development Programme, which 'began on 2 October 1952 with 55 projects'.

entries.q: Who takes the decision to conduct Panchayat elections
entries.evidence: Article 243K vests conduct in the State Election Commission, which the State Government sets up and funds; the notification/decision to hold the poll rests with the State Government (option b).

entries.q: Panchayati Raj system is in which list
entries.evidence: 'Local government (which includes the constitution and powers of panchayats ...) is Entry 5 of the State List (List II)' — Panchayati Raj is a State subject.

entries.q: Panchayati Raj subject is
entries.evidence: Same (duplicate of Q322): Entry 5, List II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule.

entries.q: By whom is the decision taken for holding Panchayat elections
entries.evidence: Same position as Q321: Art. 243K's State Election Commission conducts the poll; the State Government decides and notifies it.

entries.q: Name the committee set up by the NDC in 1957 for the reorganization of CDPs and NES
entries.evidence: 'appointed by the Government of India on 16 January 1957 to examine the working of the Community Development Program ... and the National Extension Service'. Report 24 November 1957, accepted by the NDC in January 1958.

entries.q: The chairman of the committee formed to recommend Panchayati Raj in India was
entries.evidence: 'The Chairman of this committee was Balwantrai G. Mehta'; it recommended 'democratic decentralisation', i.e. Panchayati Raj.

entries.q: Which of the following committee commissions had recommended the formation of Nyaya Panchayat
entries.evidence: 'Ashok Mehta Committee recommended the creation of Nyaya Panchayats' (report 1978).

entries.q: Who was the chairman of the committee on whose recommendation Panchayati Raj was established
entries.evidence: The 1957 committee chaired by Balwantrai Mehta recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj, accepted by the NDC in January 1958.

entries.q: Who made the recommendation of decentralization system
entries.evidence: The report 'recommended the establishment of the scheme of "democratic decentralization" which finally came to be known as Panchayati Raj'.

entries.q: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended the following
entries.verified_text: Panchayati Raj is a two-tier government
entries.evidence: Recommendation 1: 'The 3-tier system of Panchayati Raj should be replaced by the 2-tier system: Zilla Parishad ... and below it, the Mandal Panchayat'.

entries.q: Panchayat Samiti at block level is
entries.evidence: Balwantrai Mehta: 'The Panchayat Samiti should be the executive body while the Zilla Parishad should be the advisory, coordinating and supervisory body'.

entries.q: In India, the Panchayat Samiti formed at the block level is only
entries.evidence: Same recommendation: the block-level Panchayat Samiti is the executive (administrative) tier; the Zilla Parishad is supervisory.

entries.q: Under which of the following in India Panchayati Raj has the system been arranged
entries.evidence: Panchayats derive from Article 40, a Directive Principle in Part IV; the 73rd Amendment gave that directive constitutional effect.

entries.q: Under which article is the list of 29 tasks given to Panchayati Raj institutions
entries.evidence: Article 243G read with the Eleventh Schedule lists the 29 subjects.

entries.q: In which amendment of the Indian Constitution has Panchayati Raj institutions been provided constitutional status
entries.evidence: The 73rd Amendment (1992) inserted Part IX, giving Panchayati Raj constitutional status.

entries.q: On the basis of which constitutional amendment, constitutional status was provided to Panchayati Raj
entries.evidence: Same: Part IX (Arts 243-243O) was inserted by the 73rd Amendment.

entries.q: Which of the following was formed under the Panchayati Raj system
entries.evidence: The constitutional three-tier structure created by the 73rd Amendment has the Gram Panchayat at village level.

entries.q: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution directs state governments to organise village panchayats
entries.evidence: 'Article 40 is a Directive Principle ... directing the State to organise village panchayats'.

entries.q: Which of the following articles directs the State Governments to constitute Panchayats
entries.evidence: Same Article 40 directive (duplicate of Q341).

entries.q: What is the minimum age required to contest elections in Panchayati Raj institutions
entries.evidence: 'As per Article 243F of the Constitution, the minimum age for contesting Panchayat elections is 21 years'.

entries.q: Panchayati Raj in India represents
entries.evidence: Panchayati Raj embodies decentralisation, people's participation and community development — all three listed elements.

entries.q: Panchayati Raj was organized as unit of self-governance under
entries.evidence: 'The Eleventh Schedule was added by the 73rd Amendment Act of 1992' giving Panchayats constitutional status as units of self-government (Part IX).

entries.q: Panchayati Raj system in India was first started in Rajasthan and
entries.evidence: 'The first state ... was Rajasthan, inaugurated on October 2, 1959, in Nagaur district ... The second state ... was Andhra Pradesh' (11 October 1959).

entries.q: Panchayati Raj was introduced for the first time
entries.evidence: 'Rajasthan was the first state to establish Panchayati Raj on October 2, 1959 (Gandhi Jayanti) at Nagaur'.

entries.q: Panchayati Raj institutions have been given the right to control how many subjects
entries.evidence: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects devolved to Panchayats under Article 243G.

entries.q: In which state there is no Panchayat system
entries.verified_text: None of the above / More than one of the above
entries.evidence: Article 243M exempts Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram — three of the listed states (duplicate of Q313).

entries.q: In which political institution is place reserved for women in India
entries.evidence: Article 243D reserves at least one-third of Panchayat seats for women (many States now 50%); no such reservation exists for Lok Sabha or Assemblies.

entries.q: Which state/s have legalized 50% reservation for women in Panchayati Raj institutions? I. Bihar II. Uttarakhand III. Madhya Pradesh IV. Himachal Pradesh
entries.evidence: '20 States namely Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar ... Himachal Pradesh ... Madhya Pradesh ... Uttarakhand ... have made provisions of 50% reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions' — all four listed.

entries.q: Which state governments have made reservation for women in local bodies 50 percent by 2010
entries.evidence: 'Bihar was the first one to increase the reservation percentage to 50% (in Panchayats and ULBs) in 2006', with Madhya Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh following well before 2010.

entries.q: The statutory beginning of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act was given by which Constitutional Amendment Bill?
entries.evidence: '64th Amendment Bill, 1989 — Introduced by the Rajiv Gandhi government ... Passed the Lok Sabha but was defeated in the Rajya Sabha' — the precursor of the 73rd Amendment.

entries.q: Through which constitutional amendment did Panchayati Raj institutions get constitutional status
entries.evidence: Part IX (Arts 243-243O) and the Eleventh Schedule were inserted by the 73rd Amendment, 1992.

entries.q: The 73rd amendment of the Constitution is related to
entries.evidence: The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 gave Panchayati Raj constitutional status (Part IX, Arts 243-243O, Eleventh Schedule).

entries.q: A Panchayat Samiti is a Panchayati Raj structure at which level operates
entries.evidence: The three tiers are Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block/intermediate) and Zilla Parishad (district) — the Samiti is the block-level body.

entries.q: Which of the following subjects does not come under the powers of Panchayati Raj institutions
entries.evidence: The Eleventh Schedule's 29 subjects are development functions (agriculture, health, roads, poverty alleviation...) — judicial review is a High Court/Supreme Court function under Arts 226/32, not a Panchayat power.

entries.q: What does the State Government constitute every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats
entries.evidence: 'In terms of Article 243-I, the Governor shall constitute state finance commission every five years to review the financial position of the panchayats'.

entries.q: Which of the following works does not come under the jurisdiction of local self-government
entries.evidence: Local bodies handle public health, sanitation and public utilities; 'maintenance of public discipline' (policing and public order) is a State function under the State List, not a Panchayat subject.

entries.q: Which of the following was established as the first program of community development?
entries.evidence: 'The National Extension Service was inaugurated on 2nd October 1953' as the first nation-wide community-development programme; the 'Cooperation Movement' is not a CD programme — option (b), not (a).

entries.q: Which article of the Constitution of India recognizes Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language
entries.evidence: 'Article 343(1) made Hindi in Devanagari script the official language of the Union'.

entries.q: The number of recognized official languages in the Eighth List of the Indian Constitution is
entries.evidence: Options stop at 18, which was the count only between 1992 and 2003; the Eighth Schedule has listed 22 languages since the 92nd Amendment (2003) and 22 is not offered.

entries.q: Who decides the disqualification of members of State Legislative Assembly
entries.evidence: Article 192: the Governor decides disqualification questions other than those under the Tenth Schedule.

entries.q: What is the minimum percentage of votes that a party should get in the previous elections to become a national party in India?
entries.verified_text: None of the above / More than one of the above
entries.evidence: 'It secures at least 6% of valid votes in four or more states ... and wins at least 4 Lok Sabha seats' — 6% is not among the options (10%, 4%).

entries.q: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution relates to
entries.evidence: 'Tenth | Anti-defection provisions' (Arts 102(2), 191(2)) — duplicate of Q33.

entries.q: Aam Aadmi Party
entries.evidence: 'The Election Commission of India (ECI), on Monday, recognised the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) as a national party'.

entries.q: A seat of M.P. can be declared vacant if he absents himself from the house for a continuous period of
entries.evidence: Article 101(4): absence 'for a period of sixty days' without permission — two months (same rule as Q136).

entries.q: Which of the following Tax is levied by Union and collected and appropriated by States
entries.evidence: Article 268: 'Stamp duties mentioned in Union List shall be levied by Govt of India but shall be collected by States' and assigned to that State.

entries.q: After Independence, in which year were the Indian States reorganized on the linguistic basis
entries.evidence: The States Reorganisation Act 1956 redrew state boundaries on linguistic lines (14 states, 6 UTs).

entries.q: In which year did the State Jharkhand come into existence
entries.evidence: 'Jharkhand, the 28th state of India was formed on November 15, 2000'.

entries.q: Which one of the following Indian States has the largest number of members in its State Legislature?
entries.evidence: 'The current assembly consists of 68 elected members' — more than Arunachal (60), Manipur (60) and Meghalaya (60).

entries.q: Who amongst the following is a land record officer
entries.evidence: 'The patwari is the land record officer, whose job is to visit agricultural lands and maintain record of ownership and yield'.

entries.q: What is meant by 'Rule of Law'
entries.verified_text: One act for all and one judiciary for all
entries.evidence: Dicey: 'everyone, irrespective of rank and status ... shall be subjected to the same law and the same courts of the land' (duplicate of Q175).

entries.q: Which one of the following is not the characteristic of decentralization
entries.verified_text: To instil non-confidence among local communities
entries.evidence: Decentralisation is meant to build confidence and participation at the grassroots; 'instilling non-confidence' is the negation of its purpose.

entries.q: If 'One Nation One Election' is to be realized in India, which Article of the Indian Constitution has to be amended
entries.verified_text: None of the above / More than one of the above
entries.evidence: Simultaneous polls require amending both Art. 83 (term of Parliament) and Art. 172 (term of State Assemblies), so no single listed article is enough.

entries.q: Who was the Chairman of the First Law Commission in Independent India
entries.evidence: 'He also remained the Chairman of the first Law Commission of India (1955-1958)'; he was simultaneously the first Attorney-General.

entries.q: Which one of the following was established as the first programme of community development?
entries.evidence: 'The National Extension Service was inaugurated on 2nd October 1953' to staff the community-development blocks.

entries.q: What was the duration in the making of the Indian Constitution
entries.evidence: 'The Constituent Assembly of India took exactly 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days' (duplicate of Q75).

entries.q: Sikkim became a full-fledged State of the Union of India in
entries.evidence: 36th Amendment, 16 May 1975 — Sikkim became the 22nd State (duplicate of Q191/Q192).

entries.q: What is the eligibility age, after the changes made in March 2024, for senior citizens to vote by postal ballot?
entries.evidence: 'In March 2024 ... amended the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, to raise the minimum age ... from 80 years to 85 years'.

entries.q: Which pair is not correctly matched?
entries.evidence: Scheduled Areas are dealt with in the Fifth Schedule (Art. 244(1)); the Sixth Schedule covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram — so this pair is wrongly matched.

entries.q: What is true about the proceedings of the State Legislature
entries.verified_text: Business in the legislature shall be transacted only in official language of the state or in Hindi or in English
entries.evidence: 71st BPSC: option on Article 210 language of business is the true statement; Advocate General cannot vote (Article 177).

entries.q: What is true about Censure Motion
entries.evidence: BPSC's 71st Prelims final answer key deleted five questions; the sheet's CSV flags this question as deleted, consistent with the stated reasons (polity question with multiple interpretations).

entries.q: The Decentralisation System was recommended by
entries.evidence: The 1957 committee 'recommended the establishment of the scheme of democratic decentralization' — Panchayati Raj.

entries.q: Justice JS Verma Committee's report, 2013 deals with
entries.verified_text: Change in law pertaining to offences against women
entries.evidence: The committee (constituted 23 Dec 2012) was to 'recommend amendments to the Criminal Law so as to provide for quicker trial and enhanced punishment for criminals accused of committing sexual assault against women'; report 23 Jan 2013.

entries.q: Fill in the blanks. The Nehru Report was drafted by a committee headed by ..... and the subject was .....
entries.verified_text: Motilal Nehru: Constitutional arrangements in India
entries.evidence: 'The Nehru Report was drafted ... by a subcommittee formed under Motilal Nehru ... the first significant attempt by Indians to establish a constitutional framework for the country'.

entries.q: Who was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress
entries.evidence: 'In 1925 ... Kanpur ... Sarojini Naidu was elected as the President ... the first Indian woman'; Annie Besant (1917) was the first woman but not Indian.

entries.q: Who was the President of Gaya Session of the Indian National Congress held in 1922
entries.evidence: 'The Gaya Session of the Indian National Congress in 1922 was presided over by Chittaranjan Das' — after it he and Motilal Nehru founded the Swaraj Party.

entries.q: Vote on Account is meant for
entries.verified_text: Appropriating funds pending passing of the budget
entries.evidence: 'seeks a vote on account (Article 116) to cover spending until the new Lok Sabha passes a full budget' (duplicate of Q152).

entries.q: Who was elected the first President of All India Kisan Sabha at Lucknow in 1936
entries.evidence: 'Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was elected as the first president of the All India Kisan Sabha' at Lucknow, April 1936; N.G. Ranga was general secretary.

entries.q: The nation-wise breast-feeding programme "MAA" has been launched by which Union Ministry
entries.verified_text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
entries.evidence: 'MAA (Mothers' Absolute Affection) ... a nationwide programme of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare ... launched ... from August 2016'.

entries.q: Who is the highest Civil Services Officer of the Central Government
entries.evidence: 'The Cabinet Secretary: ... ex-officio Chairman of the Civil Services Board, and the senior-most civil servant in India. Occupying Rank 11 in the Indian Order of Precedence'.

entries.q: Which one of the following functions is not the concern of Local Self-Government
entries.evidence: The devolved subjects are health, sanitation, utilities and development; 'public order' is a State List police function, not a Panchayat/municipal subject.

entries.q: PURA (Providing Urban Amenities to Rural Areas) model was advocated by
entries.evidence: 'Former president Dr A.P.J Abdul Kalam coined the PURA (Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) model in 2003'.

entries.q: Who was the first Chairman of the Backward Classes Commission
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC official paper: 'Option 2 : Kaka Saheb Kalelkar' — the first Backward Classes Commission (1953) was chaired by Kaka Kalelkar; the Mandal Commission came later.

entries.q: The President
entries.verified_text: is a part of the Parliament
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q97: 'Answer. B' (Article 79 — Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses).

entries.q: Which one of the following States was never granted the Special Category Status
entries.evidence: The 11 SCS States were J&K, Assam, Nagaland, Tripura, Arunachal, Mizoram, Manipur, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh — 'the case for Special Category Status for Bihar is not made out'.

entries.q: Aam Aadmi party is a
entries.evidence: 'The poll watchdog has elevated ... Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) to national party status' — option (b), not (e).

entries.q: Which one of the following constitutional remedies is also known as 'postmortem'
entries.evidence: 'Certiorari is called the postmortem writ because it quashes an already passed illegal order.'

entries.q: Who was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress
entries.evidence: 'Annie Besant was the first woman to preside over the Congress, in 1917' (Sarojini Naidu in 1925 was the first *Indian* woman).

entries.q: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the time of partition
entries.evidence: 'J B Kripalani ... became the Congress President in 1946 and resigned from his position in 1947' — he held the office through the August 1947 partition.

entries.q: 'Rule of Law' means
entries.verified_text: One act for all and one judiciary for all
entries.evidence: Dicey's second postulate: all, 'irrespective of rank and status', subject to 'the same law and the same courts' (duplicate of Q175/Q384).

entries.q: Which is NOT a characteristic of decentralisation?
entries.evidence: Decentralisation is designed to build participation and confidence at the grassroots; the negation of that is not one of its features (duplicate of Q385).

entries.q: Which among the following is a positively charged particle
entries.evidence: 'Alpha rays are the positively charged particles' (charge +2e); beta rays are negatively charged — so (b), not (a).

entries.q: The Council of Ministers in a State is collectively responsible to
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC Q3: the Legislative Assembly (Article 164).

entries.q: The specifications required for a community to be declared as a Scheduled Tribe
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q103: 'All of the above' (the five characteristics from the Lokur Committee).

entries.q: Untouchability is abolished by which Article
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q105: 'The correct answer is (C) Article 17'.

entries.q: The Fifth Schedule deals with the governance and protection of
entries.evidence: 'Fifth | Administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes (other than NE)' — Art. 244(1).

entries.q: Under which Article(s), the Speaker can allow any member of the House to speak in his/her mother tongue
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q110: Article 120(1) proviso lets the Speaker permit a member to address the House in the mother tongue.

entries.q: Which of the following is full form of PCRA
entries.evidence: 'The full form of PCRA is Petroleum Conservation Research Association', set up under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas.

entries.q: The power to recruit the Secretarial staff of the House of the People
entries.verified_text: President after consultation with the Speaker of the House of the people
entries.evidence: 71st BPSC official paper: Article 98; the President, after consultation with the Speaker. (A studyiq key letter B is an error — the PMO has no such power.)

entries.q: Consider the following statements about Central Government: 1. Ministries and Departments are formed by the Prime Minister with consultation of the Cabinet Secretary. 2. Every Minister is allocated a Ministry by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
entries.evidence: 'Statement 1 is incorrect ... created ... under the Allocation of Business Rules ... Statement 2 is correct' (duplicate of Q83).

entries.q: What is true about the proceedings of the State Legislature
entries.verified_text: Business in the legislature shall be transacted only in official language of the state or in Hindi or in English
entries.evidence: Same 71st BPSC question as row 396, whose CSV copy keys A. Option (c) — the House may discuss a High Court judge's conduct — is barred by Article 211, so C is wrong in this option order.

entries.q: Consider the following statements: 1) The summoning of the House
entries.evidence: 71st BPSC Set H: 'Only 4' (prorogation can be effected only by the President, not by the leader of the House alone).

entries.q: Which Commission accentuated the discontent in all the political groups and paved the way for the Civil Disobedience Movement
entries.evidence: The all-British Simon Commission (arrived 3 Feb 1928) was boycotted by every major party — Congress, Muslim League, Liberals — and its rejection 'led to the launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement'.

entries.q: Who is the highest civil service officer in the Central Government
entries.evidence: Same source: the Cabinet Secretary is 'the highest-ranking civil servant in the country' (duplicate of Q410).

entries.q: When was the Planning Commission established?
entries.evidence: 'It was established on 15 March 1950, through a Cabinet Resolution of the Government of India'.

entries.q: Which of the following characteristics is not true for a central government system
entries.evidence: A unitary/centralised constitution suits small countries and is 'not suitable for big countries' (duplicate of Q20/Q177).

entries.q: Who among the following is not a permanent member of the UN Security Council
entries.evidence: 'The five permanent members are China, France, the Russian Federation, the United Kingdom, and the United States' — Germany is not one.

entries.q: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice
entries.evidence: 'The ICJ is seated in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands, making it the only principal UN organ not in New York City' — option (a) (printed 'Hung' is a garbled 'Hague').

entries.q: Amnesty International is an organization associated with
entries.evidence: 'Amnesty International is an International non-governmental organization that campaigns for human rights' (London, founded 1961).

entries.q: What is the name of China's news agency
entries.evidence: 'Xinhua News Agency ... or New China News Agency, is the official state news agency of the People's Republic of China'.

entries.q: Which country's government report is called Yellow Book
entries.evidence: 'A report drawn up by government every year ... of the French nation' — the Yellow Book of France (cf. Blue Book of Britain, White Book of Germany).

entries.q: India's first law university was established in August 1987 in
entries.evidence: 'The National Law School of India University, Bengaluru, is the first national law university established in India' — set up by Karnataka on 29 August 1987.

entries.q: When was the Border Security Force established
entries.evidence: 'On 1st December 1965, BSF was officially formed' with K.F. Rustamji as first DG.

entries.q: Who was the Chairman of the first Law Commission of independent India
entries.evidence: Setalvad was 'Chairman of the first Law Commission of India (1955-1958)' (duplicate of Q388).

entries.q: By whom is the Chairman of the State Public Service Commission appointed
entries.evidence: Article 316(1): 'in the case of a State Commission, by the Governor of the State'.

entries.q: Who was the first to receive 'Bharat Ratna'
entries.verified_text: C. Rajagopalachari (with Radhakrishnan and C.V. Raman, 1954)
entries.evidence: 'The First Bharat Ratna recipients were C. Rajagopalachari, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and C. V. Raman, who received the honour in 1954' — Rajagopalachari is the senior-most listed recipient.

entries.q: Who was the first Chairman of the Backward Castes Commission
entries.evidence: 'The First Backward Classes Commission was set up by a presidential order on 29th January 1953 under the chairmanship of Kaka Kalelkar'.

entries.q: Which is the upper house of state legislatures in India
entries.evidence: 'A Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the upper house of a state legislature' where a State is bicameral (Art. 168).

entries.q: Members of the State Legislative Council are not elected from which of the following
entries.evidence: Art. 171 electorates are local bodies, graduates, teachers and MLAs — there is no industrialists' constituency.

entries.q: What is the maximum number of members that can be in the Legislative Assembly
entries.evidence: 'Article 170: Assembly strength is 60-500' — maximum 500, minimum 60.

entries.q: Composition or dissolution of the Legislative Council in a State can be done
entries.evidence: Article 169: 'Parliament may, by law, create or abolish a Legislative Council' after the Assembly passes a special-majority resolution.

entries.q: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution provides for the election of state assemblies
entries.evidence: Article 170 provides that 'the Legislative Assembly of each State shall consist of not more than 500 and not less than 60 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies'.

entries.q: If the Speaker (Speaker) of the Legislative Assembly of a State wishes to resign, he should submit his resignation letter to.
entries.evidence: Article 179: a Speaker may resign by writing to the Deputy Speaker (and a Deputy Speaker to the Speaker).

entries.q: To whom is the Council of Ministers of the state collectively responsible
entries.evidence: Article 164(2): 'The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State'.

entries.q: By whom is the Chief Minister of a Union Territory, where such a provision exists, appointed
entries.evidence: Article 239AA(2)(a): for the NCT of Delhi 'there shall be a Council of Ministers ... in the Legislative Assembly' with the Chief Minister appointed by the President.

entries.q: The Chairman of the State Public Service Commission is appointed by
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q93: 'Answer. C' (Article 316).

entries.q: What is the retirement age of the Judges of the Supreme Court
entries.evidence: Article 124(2): a Supreme Court judge 'shall hold office until he attains the age of sixty-five years'.

entries.q: Who appoints the Judges of the Supreme Court of India
entries.evidence: 'Article 124(2) states that Supreme Court judges are appointed by the President of India through a warrant under his hand and seal'.

entries.q: Which of the following is concerned with the Supreme Court of India
entries.verified_text: More than one of the above
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC Q6: 'Ans: (D)' — appellate jurisdiction, original jurisdiction and the collegium system all relate to the Supreme Court.

entries.q: Consider the following statements about the collegium system
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q101: 'The correct answer is (D) 1 and 3'.

entries.q: In which case(s) did the Supreme Court of India give for the first time the principle of basic structure
entries.verified_text: Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala
entries.evidence: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) propounded the basic-structure doctrine — same source as Q511/Q513.

entries.q: Which one of the following subjects fall within the jurisdiction of both High Court
entries.evidence: 71st BPSC: both the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the High Courts (Article 226) protect fundamental rights.

entries.q: Supreme Court one.
entries.verified_text: None of the above / More than one of the above
entries.evidence: The Supreme Court is at once a federal court, a protector of fundamental rights and the final arbiter of the Constitution — more than one option is true, so (e).

entries.q: Sanctioned competence of judges in the Supreme Court
entries.evidence: Sanctioned strength went 18 (1977) → 26 (1986) → 31 (2009) → 34 (2019) → 38 (2026). In 1992-93 it was 26, which no printed option offers, so the option table is corrupt.

entries.q: At present, the number of judges of the Supreme Court is
entries.verified_text: None of the above / More than one of the above
entries.evidence: Sanctioned strength is 34 (CJI + 33) since 2019 and 38 by the 2026 ordinance — none of 15/25/31/20, so (e).

entries.q: Who appoints the judges in the Supreme Court of India
entries.evidence: Same provision (duplicate of Q487).

entries.q: To whom can a judge of the Supreme Court write a letter of resignation
entries.evidence: Article 124(2) proviso (a): 'a Judge may, by writing under his hand addressed to the President, resign his office'.

entries.q: What is the retirement age of Supreme Court judges
entries.evidence: Article 124(2) — 65 years (duplicate of Q486).

entries.q: Who has the power to increase the number of judges of the Supreme Court
entries.evidence: 'Article 124(1) — Parliament has power to change SC judge numbers' (Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956).

entries.q: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court propound the 'Basic Structure' doctrine
entries.evidence: 'In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala ... a 13-judge bench held by a 7:6 majority' that Parliament cannot damage the basic structure (24 April 1973).

entries.q: The decision of the Supreme Court in the Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India case is related to
entries.verified_text: Reservation of Other Backward Classes in government jobs
entries.evidence: 'The SC upheld the recommendation of Mandal commission of 27% reservation for OBCs' in government jobs (1992), with the creamy-layer exclusion.

entries.q: In which case/cases did the Supreme Court of India first give the principle of basic structure
entries.verified_text: Keshavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala
entries.evidence: Same case as Q511 (duplicate row, different spelling).

entries.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution defines the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
entries.evidence: 'Article 131 grants the Supreme Court exclusive original jurisdiction over Centre-State disputes'.

entries.q: The basis of judicial review in India is
entries.evidence: The Constitution adopts 'procedure established by law' (Art. 21), borrowed from Japan, rather than the American 'due process' — courts review against that standard.
